title: Quant-profile drift detection and sample-path aware loadbench for FP16/INT8/INT4
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a sample-path aware benchmarking harness and continuous drift detector for quantization profiles across FP16, INT8, and INT4. The goal is to measure tokens/sec and p95 under production-like mixes, detect gradual quality regressions (delta in BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity and application-specific heuristics), and surface actionable profile rollbacks or model fallbacks. This ticket focuses on the harness, metrics, alerting semantics, and a lightweight nightly runner that scans historical runs to detect drift versus a pinned golden reference.
goals: Implement loadbench that supports mixed request distributions (short-chat, long-context, batch-queries) and per-profile measurement of tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail of sequence-generation p99, and memory footprint.
Integrate quality signals: embedding cosine against golden, token-level edit-distance, and a lightweight hallucination score for open-ended prompts.

Create drift detector that runs nightly, compares current quant-profile results to golden FP16 baseline and previous run, flags regressions exceeding configurable thresholds, and opens an automated PR with diagnostics if regression is high-confidence.
Expose dashboards and automated alerts (Slack + Console) with reproducible artifact links (bench configs, seed corpus, model hashes, kernel logs).
acceptance_criteria: Loadbench can replay sample-path mix file and produce per-profile CSV with tokens_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory_max, and quality metrics for FP16/INT8/INT4.
Nightly drift job runs, stores result artifacts in s3://redwood-bench/quant-drift/2026-02-*/, and writes summary to the perf dashboard.
An alert rule triggers when quality delta > 2% absolute for embedding-similarity or when latency p95 regresses by >15% for production route SLOs.
Automated PR template with artifacts and suggested rollback to last-good profile is created when both quality and latency thresholds breached.
Docs: Confluence runbook updated with how to interpret drift alerts and manual triage steps.
implementation_notes: Harness will be based on the existing loadbench CLI but extended with: sample-path JSON input, per-request metadata tagging, and token emission timestamps for precise tokens/sec computation.
Quality signals will prioritize embedding cosine (use sentence-transformers-lite model) and a lightweight n-gram overlap for deterministic tasks to avoid full eval suite runtime overhead.
Use deterministic seeds and fixed batching policy for nightly runs to minimize variance; also record ambient GPU load and kernel selection for each run.
Store kernel selection, quant backend (FQ-int8, awq-int4 variant), and compiler flags in artifacts for root-cause regression analysis.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Nightly deterministic runs reduce noise but may miss production diurnal variation; plan to add stochastic smoke runs later.
Embedding-based quality metrics are fast but can miss semantic regressions; will keep manual weekly human spot-checks for high-risk profiles.
INT4 will show brittle regressions on some instruction sequences; risk managed by conservative alert thresholds and automatic fallback to INT8/FP16.
